messages:
mia: FYI — after yesterday's RBAC rename (editor -> content_editor) we're seeing a spike of SCIM PATCH failures for a subset of EU customers. SCIM response = 400 externalId mismatch but the provisioner logs show KMS decrypt errors too. anyone seen this pattern before?
raj: can you paste the exact log lines and an example externalId? need to see if it's Okta -> SCIM or our side
mia: sample logs:
```
2026-03-19T15:02:11Z scim-provisioner ERROR patch failed 400 {"detail":"externalId mismatch","okta_id":"00u1abc2"}
2026-03-19T15:02:11Z provisioner INFO enqueue retry user=00u1abc2 route=patch
2026-03-19T15:02:11Z kms-decrypt ERROR decrypt failed: InvalidCipherText or invalid padding
```
jules: this screams encoding/normalization. we've had users with non-breaking spaces, accented chars, and zero-width joiners in group display names before. Okta's group names sometimes come back different unicode-normalization forms; our externalId derivation used raw displayName in rollback map.
sara: +1. run a quick normalizer check; in python use:
```
import unicodedata
unicodedata.normalize('NFKC', s)
```
or on the command line try `iconv -f UTF-8 -t UTF-8//TRANSLIT` to see changes. I bet some group names changed form when the team did the rename and we didn't normalize the mapping.
eli: the KMS decrypt lines worry me — invalid padding could be corrupted ciphertext (maybe from a bad rotation) or truncated envelope. any deploys to the provisioner around 15:00?
devops-bot: deploy 2026-03-19T15:00:12Z: service=scim-provisioner image=ghcr.redwood/provisioner@sha256:abcd1234 changed dependency aws-encryption-sdk v2.4.0 -> v2.5.0
raj: that dependency change could alter envelope format if we accidentally switched provider defaults. but more likely both issues surfaced at same time (role rename + new lib) so overlapping causes.
mia: sample Okta payload (sanitized):
```
PATCH /scim/v2/Users/00u1abc2
{ "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp"],
  "Operations": [{"op":"replace","path":"roles","value": [{"value":"content_editor","displayName":"editor\u00A0"}]}]
}
```
jules: note the `\u00A0` (NBSP) — if our mapping compares to "editor" literal, that will fail. Okta sometimes stores group/display with NBSP when admins copy/paste from docs.
sara: mitigation: add a short normalization layer in the SCIM adapter to run NFKC + strip whitespace + collapse NBSP to space before mapping to role ids. can be hotpatched per-route.
eli: for KMS: check CloudTrail for Encrypt/Decrypt errors and correlation with key ARN. run `aws kms list-key-rotation-status` and check for any failed rewraps during rotation window. also check app logs for truncated ciphertext length (should be consistent envelope size).
oncall-bot: created incident INC-1234: "SCIM provisioning failures after RBAC rename + possible KMS envelope mismatch" assigned to @mia @eli
security-bot: recommended next steps: 1) run audit query for any role mapping changes in last 24h; 2) enable fallback mapping to pre-rename role IDs for 1h; 3) enqueue exponential retry for failed SCIM ops; 4) rotate provisioning key only after verifying decryption on all nodes.
mia: taking ownership. steps I'll run now: 1) backfill normalization check across active groups 2) hotpatch scim-adapter to NFKC-normalize displayName before mapping 3) run kms decrypt smoke on deployers and check CloudTrail for failures 4) kick off retry queue for impacted users. I'll update INC-1234 with findings and timeline.
raj: please dump a small sample of problematic group names (masked) and I'll run a quick `diff` against canonical role list to catch invisible chars.
sara: if we need immediate safety-net, enable a short-lived bypass that maps NBSP->space in the RBAC mapping service config, then remove after fix.
mia: will do the bypass now and post back (starting with a small canary customer). thanks everyone :thumbsup:
